title: Etale morphisms preserve topological dimension at a point
statement: Let $e:U\to V$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $u\in U$ and put $v=e(u)$. For the topological Krull dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], defined as the minimum of the Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods, one has $$\dim_u U=\dim_v V.$$ The dimensions may be infinite. No finite-type-over-a-field, Noetherian, quasi-compactness, separatedness or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For any open subscheme $W$ of $U$ or $V$, [lem-sc-scheme-sober] identifies its irreducible closed subsets with closures of single points. Thus a strict chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_n$ corresponds to distinct points $z_n\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow z_0$, where $a\rightsquigarrow b$ means $b\in\overline{\{a\}}$. Conversely such a chain gives the strict chain of singleton closures: equality of two closures would contradict uniqueness of the generic point. By [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\dim W$ is therefore the supremum of lengths of these finite strict specialization chains. This includes infinite dimension as an unbounded supremum, without choosing an infinite chain.

source.place: Tag 04N4 (lemma-dimension-at-point-local), both paragraphs: pass between irreducible closed subsets and their generic points; Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] every scheme fibre of $e$ is discrete, and [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies it homeomorphically with the set-theoretic fibre with its subspace topology. If $a\rightsquigarrow b$ and $e(a)=e(b)=v_0$, then the specialization also holds in that subspace: every open neighbourhood of $b$ there is the intersection with an ambient open neighbourhood, which contains $a$. In a discrete space take the neighbourhood $\{b\}$ to get $a=b$. Since a scheme morphism is continuous, it preserves specializations. Hence every finite strict specialization chain in any source open maps to a strict chain in any target open containing its image.

source.place: Tag 04N4, first inequality: images of generic points remain distinct because the fibres are discrete (Morphisms Tag 02GL; Schemes Tag 01K1).

proof.text: Let $B\subseteq V$ be any open neighbourhood of $v$. The inverse image $A=e^{-1}(B)$ is an open neighbourhood of $u$. Steps 1 and 2 show $\dim A\le\dim B$, by taking suprema of finite chain lengths. By [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $\dim_u U\le\dim A\le\dim B$. This holds for every $B$, so taking the minimum gives $\dim_u U\le\dim_v V$.

source.place: Tag 04N4, first inequality, conclusion from arbitrary target neighbourhoods.

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $e$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] shows that $e$ is open. For an arbitrary open neighbourhood $A\subseteq U$ of $u$, put $B=e(A)$. Then $B$ is an open neighbourhood of $v$, and $e|_A:A\to B$ is surjective on points. Fix a finite strict specialization chain $b_n\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow b_0$ in $B$ and choose $a_0\in A$ above $b_0$.

source.place: Tag 04N4, second inequality: the image of an arbitrary source neighbourhood is open, by Morphisms Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open).

proof.text: Inductively suppose $a_i\in A$ maps to $b_i$. The stalk map $R=\mathcal O_{V,b_i}\to S=\mathcal O_{U,a_i}$ is flat and local by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], the generalization $b_{i+1}$ is represented by a prime $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, since the image of $\operatorname{Spec}R\to V$ is exactly the generalizations of $b_i$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$ because the stalk map is local. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to obtain $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. Its image under $\operatorname{Spec}S\to U$ is a generalization $a_{i+1}$ of $a_i$, mapping to $b_{i+1}$: the canonical maps commute with $e$, as on affine charts they are the localized ring maps in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Opens contain every generalization of each of their points, so $a_{i+1}\in A$. The lift is distinct from $a_i$ because $b_{i+1}\ne b_i$. This finite induction lifts the entire strict chain inside $A$.

source.place: Tag 04N4, second inequality: flat local stalk map, Schemes Tag 01J7 (lemma-specialize-points), and flat going down, Algebra Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down).

proof.text: Step 5 and the chain description of step 1 give $\dim B\le\dim A$ for every source neighbourhood $A$ of $u$. Since $B=e(A)$ is an open neighbourhood of $v$, [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim_v V\le\dim B\le\dim A$. Taking the minimum over $A$ gives $\dim_v V\le\dim_u U$. Combine with step 3 by antisymmetry. All comparisons use suprema of finite chains and minima in the extended natural numbers, so the argument also covers dimension $\infty$.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04N4 (lemma-dimension-at-point-local), complete proof: inject specialization chains using discrete fibres, lift chains using flat going down, and take neighbourhood minima.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q156-048e7823b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, a six-step split of Stacks 04N4 (descent.tex, lemma-dimension-at-point-local) that creates no new nodes. The statement matches the source exactly: e étale, dim_u U = dim_v V, with dimension at a point defined as the minimum over open neighbourhoods (Topology 0055 (4)). No hypothesis is added, and infinite dimension is allowed. Step 1: by uniqueness of generic points (lem-sc-scheme-sober, 01IS), strict chains of irreducible closed sets are the same as chains of distinct specializing points. Step 2: fibres are discrete (02GL (2)) and homeomorphic to the set-theoretic fibre (01K1, a clause of def-pc-scheme-fibre), so a specialization between two points with the same image is trivial, and images of strict chains stay strict. Step 3: the first inequality, from minima over A = e^{-1}(B). Step 4: e is open by lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open (01UA), so B = e(A) is open. Step 5: chains are lifted one generalization at a time using the flat local stalk map, clause (1) and the localization formula of lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism (01J7), and going down (00HS). The induction has a base and a step, the square of canonical maps commutes on affine charts, and lifts stay in A because opens are stable under generalization. Step 6: the reverse inequality. Every cited statement says what its step uses, proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and there is no cycle. Edge cases checked: empty U, a finite separable point, D(t) ⊂ A¹ (not surjective), an infinite disjoint union (not quasi-compact), infinite dimension, and topological versus local-ring dimension. No existing node states 04N4, and Mathlib has nothing comparable (grep for topologicalKrullDim). Accepted tool uses: lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points and lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism, both from sk-thm-p1 and used only as generic scheme facts.
